title: Carrot Cake Pancakes with Maple Yoghurt
changes_from_base: Grated carrot, pecans and warm spices go into a half-wholemeal batter made with Greek yoghurt and coconut oil, served with a maple yoghurt topping.
summary: Warmly spiced pancakes packed with grated carrot and toasted pecans, topped with a maple yoghurt dollop that echoes classic carrot cake.
equipment: wire rack set in a rimmed baking tray

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
coconut oil, softened or melted, plus more for the pan
maple syrup (2-3 tsp), plus more to serve

steps.title: Whisk Dry
steps.text: Whisk 120 g plain flour, 113 g white wholemeal flour, 50 g caster sugar, 1 tsp baking powder, 1 tsp bicarbonate of soda, 1 tsp cinnamon, ½ tsp ginger, ½ tsp salt and ¼ tsp nutmeg.

steps.title: Whisk Wet
steps.text: Whisk 300 ml warm milk, 152 g Greek yoghurt, 57 g coconut oil, 2 tsp vanilla and 1 egg yolk, keeping the white aside.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Pour the wet mix into the dry and whisk just until combined with small lumps, then stir in 198 g grated carrots, 53 g toasted chopped pecans and 27 g cinnamon baking chips if using, and rest the batter, uncovered, 15 min.

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Heat a large non-stick pan over medium heat and the oven to 93°C, then gently stir the egg white into the batter.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Grease the pan with 1-1½ tsp coconut oil and drop 60 ml portions of batter, cooking until the bases are brown and firm enough to flip, 2-3 min.

steps.title: Flip
steps.text: Flip and cook until brown, a further 1-2 min, keeping cooked pancakes warm on a rack in the oven and repeating with the rest of the batter.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Stir 57 g Greek yoghurt with 2-3 tsp maple syrup and 2-3 tsp milk, then serve the pancakes with a dollop of this topping, extra maple syrup and chopped pecans.

tips: Let the batter rest for 15 min so the grated carrot can soften slightly before cooking.
Wait until the base is firm before flipping, or the pancakes may stick and break.
Freeze any extras flat so they reheat evenly in the oven or toaster later.
storage: Cool any leftovers and freeze them airtight for up to 3 months, then reheat in a 175°C oven or a toaster. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
